objects.definition: typedef uint64_t ecs_id_t;
objects.description: Opaque 64-bit identifier for anything that can be added to an entity (entity ids, pairs, with optional flags).

objects.definition: typedef ecs_id_t ecs_entity_t;
objects.description: Alias of ecs_id_t that represents entity identifiers (lower 32 bits id, upper 32 bits generation).
Simple contiguous list of component ids describing an archetype/type. Used for table composition and descriptors.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_world_t ecs_world_t;
objects.description: Opaque world/context object that owns all ECS state, storage, systems and queries.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_stage_t ecs_stage_t;
objects.description: Opaque staging context that allows deferring operations and multithreaded mutation.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_table_t ecs_table_t;
objects.description: Opaque archetype/table storing entities that share the same ecs_type_t.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_term_t ecs_term_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration alias updated later by struct definition; represents a single query constraint/term.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_query_t ecs_query_t;
objects.description: Opaque/then-defined query object that matches entities against a list of ecs_term_t constraints.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_observer_t ecs_observer_t;
objects.description: Opaque/then-defined observer that reacts to events when its query matches.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_observable_t ecs_observable_t;
objects.description: Opaque observable producer of events (currently the world).

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_iter_t ecs_iter_t;
objects.description: Iterator state and view over current match for iterable objects (queries, each, children, etc.).

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_ref_t ecs_ref_t;
objects.description: Opaque ref that caches lookup info for an entity+component for fast repeated access.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_type_hooks_t ecs_type_hooks_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration alias updated later by struct definition; holds component lifecycle hooks and related callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_type_info_t ecs_type_info_t;
objects.description: Forward declaration alias updated later by struct definition; holds size, alignment and hooks for a component id.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_record_t ecs_record_t;
objects.description: Opaque per-entity record with table/row info used internally and by fast paths.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_component_record_t ecs_component_record_t;
objects.description: Opaque per-(component) id metadata such as type info and table references.

objects.definition: typedef void ecs_poly_t;
objects.description: Generic poly base type for polymorphic Flecs objects that support mixins (world, stage, query).

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_mixins_t ecs_mixins_t;
objects.description: Opaque mixin table descriptor for poly objects, storing offsets to optional mixins.
Common header embedded in poly objects for runtime type checking, refcounting and mixin access.

objects.definition: typedef struct ecs_table_record_t ecs_table_record_t;
objects.description: Opaque info describing where a field/id lives inside a table and how to access it.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_run_action_t)(
    ecs_iter_t *it);
objects.description: Function pointer type for overriding how to iterate/invoke a runnable (systems/observers).

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_iter_action_t)(
    ecs_iter_t *it);
objects.description: Callback invoked for an iterator result (per matched table/batch).

objects.definition:
typedef bool (*ecs_iter_next_action_t)(
    ecs_iter_t *it);
objects.description: Function pointer stored in iterators to progress them regardless of origin.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_iter_fini_action_t)(
    ecs_iter_t *it);
objects.description: Callback to free iterator resources when iteration ends early.
Comparator for ordering entities by a component value.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_sort_table_action_t)(
    ecs_world_t* world,
    ecs_table_t* table,
    ecs_entity_t* entities,
    void* ptr,
    int32_t size,
    int32_t lo,
    int32_t hi,
    ecs_order_by_action_t order_by);
objects.description: Callback to sort a single table range by a component, given comparator.

objects.definition:
typedef uint64_t (*ecs_group_by_action_t)(
    ecs_world_t *world,
    ecs_table_t *table,
    ecs_id_t group_id,
    void *ctx);
objects.description: Computes a group id for a table to group query results.

objects.definition:
typedef void* (*ecs_group_create_action_t)(
    ecs_world_t *world,
    uint64_t group_id,
    void *group_by_ctx);
objects.description: Callback when a new query group is created; returns per-group context.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_group_delete_action_t)(
    ecs_world_t *world,
    uint64_t group_id,
    void *group_ctx,
    void *group_by_ctx);
objects.description: Callback when a query group is deleted; receives contexts for cleanup.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_module_action_t)(
    ecs_world_t *world);
objects.description: Initializer for modules to register components/systems into a world.
Callback executed on world exit or in post-frame actions with user ctx.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_ctx_free_t)(
    void *ctx);
objects.description: Generic deallocator function type for user contexts.
Comparator for plain values (not entity-aware).

objects.definition:
typedef uint64_t (*ecs_hash_value_action_t)(
    const void *ptr);
objects.description: Hasher for plain values.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_xtor_t)(
    void *ptr,
    int32_t count,
    const ecs_type_info_t *type_info);
objects.description: Ctor/dtor signature for bulk-constructing/destructing component arrays.
Copy hook for components (assignment copy of count elements).

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ecs_move_t)(
    void *dst_ptr,
    void *src_ptr,
    int32_t count,
    const ecs_type_info_t *type_info);
objects.description: Move hook for components, can destruct/move-from src.
Three-way comparator hook for components.
Equality predicate hook for components.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*flecs_poly_dtor_t)(
    ecs_poly_t *poly);
objects.description: Destructor for poly objects.
Access qualifier for term fields indicating read/write behavior and filtering.
Logical operator for how a term should contribute to matching.
Policy for query caching (none, auto, all, or default based on context).
Reference in a term to an entity or variable by id or name, with flags encoded on the id field.
Fully specified term of a query, including id or decomposed pair refs, traversal relationship, access and operator.
Query object with compiled terms, field metadata, caching policy, contexts and owning world info.
Observer with associated query and event set; invokes callbacks on matching events; holds contexts and observable.
Lifecycle hooks and optional event callbacks for a component type, with hook/legality flags and user/binding contexts.
Runtime type information for a component id: size, alignment, hooks, owning component id and optional name.
Utility holding a dynamic typed value pointer with its type id.
Descriptor to create or find an entity, set parent/name/symbol, add ids and set component values.
Descriptor for bulk create/populate of entities in a table with optional provided ids and data arrays.
Descriptor to find/create a component entity and register its type info (size, hooks, alignment).
Iterator state for any iterable (query/each/children/page/worker). Stores current table match, field metadata, timing and callbacks.
Descriptor to create a query: terms array or expression, caching policy, ordering/grouping callbacks and contexts.
Descriptor to create an observer: embeds a query desc, event set, run/callback functions and contexts.
Parameters for emitting/enqueuing an event to observers, including ids, optional table/range, and context.
Describes compile-time configuration and version of the Flecs build.
Snapshot of runtime statistics, counters and configuration for a world, including timing, counts and command stats.
Info about a query group, including matches, table count, and per-group context.
Builtin component storing identifier strings for name/symbol/alias with cached hashes and index pointer.
Builtin component describing size and alignment of a component id.
Builtin component holding a pointer to a poly object stored on an entity.
Hint component indicating which component to use by default when setting a value on a child without specifying component.
Return type that provides a view over all entity ids in a world and how many are alive.
Configuration for cleaning up empty tables with separate clear and delete generations and time budget.
Counts returned by ecs_query_count: number of results, entities, and optionally tables.
Referenced type used by range APIs is not defined in this header. Information missing.
Private iterator internals type referenced by ecs_iter_t; defined in private headers, not in this file.
Bitset type used in queries/iterators for field masks; definition not present in this header.
Size type used throughout; definition not present in this header (likely typedef).
16-bit flags type; definition not present in this header (from private/api_defines.h).
32-bit flags type used by many APIs; not defined here (from private headers).
64-bit flags type used for constrained vars and traversal flags; not defined here.

functions.name: ecs_init
functions.description: Create a new world with all enabled addons imported automatically. Returns a new ecs_world_t instance.
requirements: Must be paired with ecs_fini to release resources when done.
Not thread-safe to create from multiple threads simultaneously against the same global state (typical C library expectation).

functions.name: ecs_mini
functions.description: Create a new minimal world with just the core module (no addon imports).
requirements: Must be paired with ecs_fini to release resources.

functions.name: ecs_init_w_args
functions.description: Create a new world passing command line arguments. Used to derive app name from argv[0] and other runtime opts.
requirements: argv must be a valid array of char* of length argc (or greater) and live at least for the duration of the call.
Must be paired with ecs_fini to release resources.

functions.name: ecs_fini
functions.description: Destroy a world and free all associated resources.
requirements: world must be a valid ecs_world_t* obtained from ecs_init/ecs_mini/ecs_init_w_args or a stage created with ecs_stage_new (for which this function is not intended).
Should not be called concurrently with other operations on the same world.
After call, world pointer becomes invalid.

functions.name: ecs_is_fini
functions.description: Return whether the world is in the process of being destroyed.
requirements: world must be a valid pointer to a world or stage.

functions.name: ecs_atfini
functions.description: Register a callback to be executed when the world is destroyed.
requirements: world must be valid.
action must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked with (world, ctx) near world shutdown.
Must be registered before ecs_fini starts.

functions.name: ecs_get_entities
functions.description: Return a struct containing an array of all entity ids in the world, and counts for total and alive ids. The returned array is owned by the world and may change when entities are created/deleted.
requirements: world must be valid.
Do not mutate or free the returned ids pointer.
Array content may become invalid after further entity creation/deletion; copy if needed.

functions.name: ecs_world_get_flags
functions.description: Return internal flags set on the world (for diagnostics/debugging).
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_frame_begin
functions.description: Begin a frame for applications that do not use ecs_progress; enables FPS limiting/time measurements. Returns the provided or measured delta time.
requirements: Must be followed by ecs_frame_end for each begin.
Call from main thread only.
world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_frame_end
functions.description: End a frame previously started with ecs_frame_begin.
requirements: Must be called after a matching ecs_frame_begin.
world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_run_post_frame
functions.description: Schedule an action to be executed once after the current frame finishes (post-frame).
requirements: world must be valid.
action must be a valid function pointer. The action is called with (world, ctx).

functions.name: ecs_quit
functions.description: Signal the application should quit; causes ecs_progress to return false.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_should_quit
functions.description: Return whether a quit has been requested.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_measure_frame_time
functions.description: Enable or disable frame time measurements.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_measure_system_time
functions.description: Enable or disable per-system time measurements.
requirements: world must be valid.
Enabling adds per-system overhead.

functions.name: ecs_set_target_fps
functions.description: Set target frames per second for ecs_progress frame pacing.
requirements: world must be valid.
fps should be > 0 to limit; 0 disables limiting.

functions.name: ecs_set_default_query_flags
functions.description: Set default flags applied to new query/filter descriptors in addition to descriptor flags.
requirements: world must be valid.
flags should be a combination of EcsQuery* flags.

functions.name: ecs_readonly_begin
functions.description: Enter readonly mode. Disallows mutations; in multi_threaded=true, disallows all world mutations. Returns whether world is now readonly.
requirements: Must be paired with ecs_readonly_end.
Call only from a context that has exclusive world access.
During readonly, use stages for deferred ECS operations.

functions.name: ecs_readonly_end
functions.description: Exit readonly mode and flush deferred operations from stages.
requirements: Must be called after ecs_readonly_begin.
world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_merge
functions.description: Merge all commands enqueued for a stage back into the world.
requirements: stage must be a stage world pointer (ecs_get_stage/ecs_stage_new).
Not required for main world pointer.

functions.name: ecs_defer_begin
functions.description: Begin deferring operations until end of frame. Returns true if world switched from non-deferred to deferred.
requirements: Must be paired with ecs_defer_end.
Thread-safe.

functions.name: ecs_defer_end
functions.description: End deferring operations. Returns true if world switched from deferred to non-deferred.
requirements: Must follow ecs_defer_begin.
Thread-safe.

functions.name: ecs_defer_suspend
functions.description: Temporarily suspend deferring without flushing the queue to perform an undeferred operation.
requirements: Must be called while deferring is enabled.
Should be followed by ecs_defer_resume before ecs_defer_end.

functions.name: ecs_defer_resume
functions.description: Resume deferring after ecs_defer_suspend.
requirements: Must be called after ecs_defer_suspend and before ecs_defer_end.

functions.name: ecs_is_deferred
functions.description: Return whether deferring is enabled for current stage.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_is_defer_suspended
functions.description: Return whether deferring is currently suspended for current stage.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_set_stage_count
functions.description: Configure world to have N stages for multi-threading/deferred queues.
requirements: world must be valid.
stages >= 1.

functions.name: ecs_get_stage_count
functions.description: Get the number of configured stages.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_get_stage
functions.description: Get a stage handle (as ecs_world_t*) for the given stage index.
requirements: world must be valid.
stage_id must be in [0, ecs_get_stage_count(world)).

functions.name: ecs_stage_is_readonly
functions.description: Return whether the provided world/stage is in readonly mode.
requirements: world or stage must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_stage_new
functions.description: Create an unmanaged stage whose lifecycle must be freed manually.
requirements: world must be valid.
Free with ecs_stage_free.

functions.name: ecs_stage_free
functions.description: Free an unmanaged stage created with ecs_stage_new.
requirements: stage must be a stage returned by ecs_stage_new.
Must not be used after freeing.

functions.name: ecs_stage_get_id
functions.description: Get stage id for the provided stage/world.
requirements: world must be valid (stage or world).

functions.name: ecs_set_ctx
functions.description: Associate a user context pointer with the world with optional destructor.
requirements: world must be valid.
ctx_free, if non-NULL, will be called with ctx when the world is freed.

functions.name: ecs_set_binding_ctx
functions.description: Set binding-specific context pointer with optional destructor for language bindings.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_get_ctx
functions.description: Get the user context pointer associated with the world.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_get_binding_ctx
functions.description: Get the binding context pointer associated with the world.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_get_build_info
functions.description: Return build-time info about Flecs (compiler, addons, flags, version, etc).

functions.name: ecs_get_world_info
functions.description: Return a pointer to a struct with runtime world statistics and configuration.
requirements: world must be valid.
Returned pointer remains valid while the world exists; do not free.

functions.name: ecs_dim
functions.description: Preallocate memory for at least entity_count entities.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity_count >= 0.

functions.name: ecs_shrink
functions.description: Free unused memory in world (pages, columns, empty tables). Does not free internal allocator pools unless built with FLECS_USE_OS_ALLOC.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_set_entity_range
functions.signature: void ecs_set_entity_range(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t id_start, ecs_entity_t id_end);
functions.description: Constrain issued entity ids to [id_start, id_end). If id_end is 0, range is infinite.
requirements: world must be valid.
If id_end != 0 then id_end > id_start.
Application aborts if new id would equal id_end.

functions.name: ecs_enable_range_check
functions.description: Enable/disable range checking for range-limited entities on a stage.
requirements: world must be valid.
Returns previous value.

functions.name: ecs_get_max_id
functions.description: Return largest issued entity id (without generation).
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_run_aperiodic
functions.description: Force aperiodic actions (delayed internal maintenance). Pass 0 to run all.
requirements: world must be valid.
flags should be a combination of EcsAperiodic* flags (internal).

functions.name: ecs_delete_empty_tables
functions.description: Clean up empty tables according to generation and optional time budget. Returns number of deleted tables.
requirements: world must be valid.
desc must be a valid pointer; fields control clear/delete and time budget.

functions.name: ecs_get_world
functions.description: Get world from a poly object.
requirements: poly must be a valid poly object (world/stage/query/etc).

functions.name: ecs_get_entity
functions.description: Get entity associated with a poly object.
requirements: poly must be a valid poly object that has an associated entity.

functions.name: flecs_poly_is_
functions.description: Return true if the poly object is of specified type (compare against type magic).
requirements: object must be a valid poly pointer.
type must be a valid magic value for a supported poly type.

functions.name: ecs_make_pair
functions.description: Construct a pair id from first (relationship) and second (target) entities.
requirements: first and second are entity ids (may be 0 for specific uses only if allowed by API patterns; generally both non-zero).

functions.name: ecs_exclusive_access_begin
functions.description: Begin exclusive access from the calling thread; other threads accessing world will panic (assert builds).
requirements: world must be valid.
Must be paired with ecs_exclusive_access_end from the same thread.
thread_name must remain valid (not copied) while exclusive access is held.
Only call once per thread while active.

functions.name: ecs_exclusive_access_end
functions.description: End exclusive access. Optionally keep world locked against mutations (readonly allowed) until exclusive access is begun again.
requirements: Must be called from the same thread that called ecs_exclusive_access_begin.
If lock_world is true, subsequent mutations are blocked until another begin/end.
Calling on a world with another thread owning exclusive access will panic.

functions.name: ecs_new
functions.description: Create a new empty entity id (ignores scope/with).
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_new_low_id
functions.description: Create a new low id (reserved range for components, non-recycled).
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_new_w_id
functions.description: Create a new entity optionally with the specified (component) id.
requirements: world must be valid.
component may be 0 to add none; otherwise must be a valid id.

functions.name: ecs_new_w_table
functions.description: Create a new entity in the specified table.
requirements: world and table must be valid.
table must belong to the same world.

functions.name: ecs_entity_init
functions.description: Find or create an entity using the descriptor (name, id, parent, sets/adds).
requirements: world must be valid.
desc must be non-NULL with _canary == 0.
If both desc->entity and desc->name are provided, names must match or the call fails.
If desc->use_low_id true and no id specified, new id will be low id.
desc->add/desc->set arrays must be 0-terminated when provided.

functions.name: ecs_bulk_init
functions.description: Bulk create or populate entities into a single table. Returns pointer to array of entity ids (owned by internal storage if not provided by desc).
requirements: world must be valid.
desc must be non-NULL with _canary == 0.
If desc->entities is provided, those entities must be empty (no components).
desc->ids up to FLECS_ID_DESC_MAX define table composition; if table is provided, ids must match table type when data supplied.
desc->data entries align with ids array; NULL allowed for tags or to skip setting a component.
Returned pointer may point to internal storage subject to invalidation if entities are created/deleted; copy if needed.

functions.name: ecs_bulk_new_w_id
functions.signature: const ecs_entity_t* ecs_bulk_new_w_id(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_id_t component, int32_t count);
functions.description: Create count entities with an optional single (component) id and return pointer to the first id in a contiguous array.
requirements: world must be valid.
count >= 0.
component may be 0 to add none.

functions.name: ecs_clone
functions.signature: ecs_entity_t ecs_clone(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t dst, ecs_entity_t src, bool copy_value);
functions.description: Clone components from src into dst (or create a new entity if dst == 0). Optionally copy component values.
requirements: world must be valid.
src must be a valid/alive entity to clone from.
If src has a name, it's not copied to dst.
If copy_value is true, components must have copy hooks or be trivially copyable.

functions.name: ecs_delete
functions.description: Delete an entity and its components; id becomes available for recycling.
requirements: world must be valid.
Safe to call on non-alive entity (no side effects).

functions.name: ecs_delete_with
functions.description: Delete all entities (tables) that have the specified id (may be wildcard/pair).
requirements: world must be valid.
component must be a valid id (wildcards allowed).

functions.name: ecs_set_child_order
functions.signature: void ecs_set_child_order(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t parent, const ecs_entity_t *children, int32_t child_count);
functions.description: Set explicit child order for a parent with the EcsOrderedChildren tag, using the provided children array.
requirements: world must be valid.
parent must have EcsOrderedChildren, else the operation fails.
children must be a valid array of length child_count with entity ids that are children of parent.
Operation is immediate and not deferred; calling from multithreaded systems will fail.

functions.name: ecs_get_ordered_children
functions.description: Get ordered children array for a parent with EcsOrderedChildren.
requirements: world must be valid.
parent must have EcsOrderedChildren else the operation fails.
Returned ids pointer is owned by world; do not modify/free.

functions.name: ecs_add_id
functions.signature: void ecs_add_id(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Add a (component) id to an entity; no-op if already present.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid/alive to have components added.
component must be a valid id.

functions.name: ecs_remove_id
functions.signature: void ecs_remove_id(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Remove a (component) id from an entity; no-op if not present.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid/alive.
component must be a valid id.

functions.name: ecs_auto_override_id
functions.signature: void ecs_auto_override_id(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Configure an auto-override for a component on a prefab/base so instances automatically override that component on instantiation.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity should be the base (e.g., prefab) receiving auto override.
component must be a valid id.

functions.name: ecs_clear
functions.description: Remove all components from an entity (does not delete the entity).
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid/alive.

functions.name: ecs_remove_all
functions.description: Remove all instances of the specified id from all entities/tables (wildcard/pairs allowed).
requirements: world must be valid.
component must be a valid id (wildcards allowed).

functions.name: ecs_set_with
functions.description: Set a default (component) id to be added to entities created with ecs_entity_init. Returns previously set component.
requirements: world must be valid.
Only one component can be set at a time; new call overrides prior default.

functions.name: ecs_get_with
functions.description: Get the component set with ecs_set_with.
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_enable
functions.signature: void ecs_enable(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, bool enabled);
functions.description: Enable or disable an entity by adding/removing EcsDisabled tag.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid/alive.

functions.name: ecs_enable_id
functions.signature: void ecs_enable_id(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component, bool enable);
functions.description: Enable or disable a component on an entity without removing it (affects query matching).
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid/alive.
component must be a valid id (and component must support toggling to be meaningful).

functions.name: ecs_is_enabled_id
functions.signature: bool ecs_is_enabled_id(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Return whether a component is currently enabled on the entity.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid.
component must be a valid id.

functions.name: ecs_get_id
functions.signature: const void* ecs_get_id(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Get const pointer to component data on an entity; may resolve inherited components via IsA.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid.
component must be a valid id.
Returned pointer is only valid until structural change of the entity/table.

functions.name: ecs_get_mut_id
functions.signature: void* ecs_get_mut_id(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Get mutable pointer to component data, not resolving inherited components.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid.
component must be a valid id.
Returned pointer is only valid until structural change of the entity/table.
Do not modify inherited/shared data; this API does not return inherited values.

functions.name: ecs_ensure_id
functions.signature: void* ecs_ensure_id(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component, size_t size);
functions.description: Ensure the entity has the component, returning mutable pointer. Adds component if missing.
requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid/alive.
component must be a valid id with data of given size.
If called in deferred/readonly mode and component does not exist, may return temporary storage; call ecs_modified_id after writing.

functions.name: ecs_ref_init_id

functions.name: ecs_get_version

functions.name: ecs_type_str

functions.name: ecs_table_str

functions.name: ecs_entity_str

requirements: world must be valid.
entity must be valid.
Free returned string with ecs_os_free.

functions.name: ecs_has_id
functions.signature: bool ecs_has_id(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Return whether entity has or inherits the (component) id.

functions.name: ecs_owns_id

functions.description: Return whether entity directly owns the component id (not inherited).

entity and component must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_get_target
functions.signature: ecs_entity_t ecs_get_target(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_entity_t rel, int32_t index);

index >= 0.

functions.name: ecs_get_parent

entity must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_get_target_for_id
functions.signature: ecs_entity_t ecs_get_target_for_id(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_entity_t rel, ecs_id_t component);

functions.signature: int32_t ecs_get_depth(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, ecs_entity_t rel);
functions.description: Return depth in relationship tree by counting targets traversing up rel. Only acyclic relationships supported.

functions.name: ecs_count_id
functions.description: Return number of entities that have the specified id.

entity must be a valid id (component/pair).

functions.name: ecs_get_name
functions.signature: const char* ecs_get_name(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity);

functions.name: ecs_get_symbol
functions.signature: const char* ecs_get_symbol(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity);

requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_set_name
functions.signature: ecs_entity_t ecs_set_name(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, const char *name);

functions.name: ecs_set_symbol
functions.signature: ecs_entity_t ecs_set_symbol(ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t entity, const char *symbol);
functions.description: Set or overwrite entity symbol; if entity==0, creates a new entity and sets the symbol.

symbol must be a valid string (copied).

functions.name: ecs_set_alias

functions.name: ecs_lookup_child

name must be a valid string.

functions.signature: ecs_entity_t ecs_lookup_path_w_sep(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t parent, const char *path, const char *sep, const char *prefix, bool recursive);

functions.name: ecs_lookup_symbol
functions.signature: ecs_entity_t ecs_lookup_symbol(const ecs_world_t *world, const char *symbol, bool lookup_as_path, bool recursive);

symbol must be a valid string.

functions.name: ecs_get_path_w_sep
functions.signature: char* ecs_get_path_w_sep(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t parent, ecs_entity_t child, const char *sep, const char *prefix);

functions.name: ecs_get_path_w_sep_buf
functions.signature: void ecs_get_path_w_sep_buf(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_entity_t parent, ecs_entity_t child, const char *sep, const char *prefix, ecs_strbuf_t *buf, bool escape);

functions.name: ecs_new_from_path_w_sep

path must be a valid string.

functions.name: ecs_set_scope

functions.name: ecs_get_scope

functions.name: ecs_set_name_prefix
functions.description: Set name prefix used for registering names (e.g., strip C prefixes). Returns previous prefix.

prefix string must remain valid until copied internally (implementation-defined).

functions.description: Set 0-terminated search path (entity ids) used by lookup operations; returns current lookup path.

functions.name: ecs_get_lookup_path
functions.description: Get current lookup path array (0-terminated).
requirements: world must be valid.

functions.name: ecs_component_init

functions.name: ecs_get_type_info
functions.signature: const ecs_type_info_t* ecs_get_type_info(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_id_t component);
functions.description: Return type info (size, alignment, hooks, name) for a component or pair id.

functions.description: Register lifecycle hooks (ctor/dtor/copy/move/etc) for a component before it is used.

functions.description: Return the component entity associated with a component/pair id, following rules for tags and pairs (may return 0).

functions.description: Return internal flags associated with id, or 0 if id not in use.

functions.description: Convert id flags (PAIR, TOGGLE, AUTO_OVERRIDE) to string; returns NULL if none/invalid.

functions.name: ecs_id_str
functions.description: Convert id to human-readable string (including flags and pairs). Caller must free with ecs_os_free.

Free returned string with ecs_os_free.

functions.name: ecs_id_str_buf
functions.signature: void ecs_id_str_buf(const ecs_world_t *world, ecs_id_t component, ecs_strbuf_t *buf);

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: generic text string
# Used by many APIs as names/symbols/aliases/expressions. We should generate
# interesting but valid C strings (UTF-8 bytes) that cover:
# - Empty and very short strings
# - Typical identifier-like names
# - Paths with separators '/', '.', '::'
# - Names with spaces and punctuation
# - Unicode characters (multi-byte UTF-8)
# - Longish names but keep under 4096 bytes total
# - Strings that look like variable assignments or query args for ecs_query_args_parse
# The fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times; the harness typically
# consumes from a single buffer. We therefore concatenate multiple candidate
# strings with length prefixes so the harness can slice them deterministically.
# Format we emit:
# [count:1 byte][entry1_len:2 bytes LE][entry1 bytes]...[entryN]
# Each entry is a UTF-8 string without NUL terminator. Harnesses commonly read
# the raw bytes; to ensure valid C strings, we avoid NUL within entries.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_ENTRIES = 32

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "名前",        # Japanese
    "имя",         # Russian
    "اسم",         # Arabic
    "πρόγραμμα",   # Greek
    "nombre",      # Latin
    "名字/子",     # CJK with slash
    "路径/子/节点",  # Path-like unicode
    "α::β::γ",     # Namespace-ish
]

PUNCT_SETS = [
    "-_.",
    "-_.:/",
    "-_.:/@#",
    "-_.:/@#()[]{}",
]

QUERY_ARG_TEMPLATES = [
    "(a: 1, b: 2)",
    "x: true, y: false",
    "name: '%ID%', path: '%PATH%'",
    "(entity: %ID%, group: 42)",
    "first: '%SYM%', second: '%SYM2%'",
    "limit: 10, offset: 5",
]

PATH_SEPS = ["/", ".", "::"]

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_BODY = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    s += "".join(rng.choice(IDENT_BODY) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sep = rng.choice(PATH_SEPS)
    parts = [_rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 10)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5))]
    return sep.join(parts)


def _rand_symbol(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Symbols often allow broader chars; avoid NUL
    base = _rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 12))
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        punct = rng.choice(PUNCT_SETS)
        tail = "".join(rng.choice(IDENT_BODY + punct) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 8)))
        return base + tail
    return base


def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    s = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    # Occasionally mix with ASCII
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = _rand_path(rng) + rng.choice(["/", ".", "::"]) + s
    return s


def _rand_query_args(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tmpl = rng.choice(QUERY_ARG_TEMPLATES)
    return (tmpl
            .replace("%ID%", str(rng.randint(1, 100000)))
            .replace("%PATH%", _rand_path(rng))
            .replace("%SYM%", _rand_symbol(rng))
            .replace("%SYM2%", _rand_symbol(rng)))


def _make_entries(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure coverage of varied categories
    basics = [
        "",  # empty
        "a",  # single char
        "0",  # numeric
        "_",  # underscore
    ]
    entries.extend(s.encode('utf-8') for s in basics)

    # Identifiers and paths
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        entries.append(_rand_ident(rng).encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        entries.append(_rand_path(rng).encode('utf-8'))

    # Symbols and aliases
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        entries.append(_rand_symbol(rng).encode('utf-8'))

    # Unicode-rich names
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        entries.append(_rand_unicode(rng).encode('utf-8'))

    # Query-arg like expressions (for ecs_query_args_parse)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        entries.append(_rand_query_args(rng).encode('utf-8'))

    # Longer descriptive names with spaces/punctuation
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        words = [_rand_ident(rng, 3, 10) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))]
        punct = rng.choice([" ", " - ", "/", ": "])
        entries.append(punct.join(words).encode('utf-8'))

    # Trim entries count
    if len(entries) > MAX_ENTRIES:
        rng.shuffle(entries)
        entries = entries[:MAX_ENTRIES]

    # Enforce each entry non-empty of NUL (already ensured), cap length
    capped: List[bytes] = []
    for e in entries:
        if len(e) > 512:
            e = e[:512]
        # Replace any accidental NULs defensively (shouldn't happen)
        if b"\x00" in e:
            e = e.replace(b"\x00", b"_")
        capped.append(e)
    return capped


def _pack(entries: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Pack as: count(1 byte) + repeated [len(2 bytes LE) + data]
    out = bytearray()
    cnt = min(len(entries), 255)
    out.append(cnt)
    for i in range(cnt):
        s = entries[i]
        ln = min(len(s), 0xFFFF)
        out += ln.to_bytes(2, 'little')
        out += s[:ln]
        if len(out) >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    entries = _make_entries(rng)
    buf = _pack(entries)
    # Guarantee non-empty buffer
    if not buf:
        return b"\x00\x00\x00"
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid and interesting entity path strings for Flecs APIs that
# accept names/paths with separators and optional root prefixes.
# - Should cover single identifiers, multi-segment paths, escaped/separator variations,
#   aliases/prefixes, Unicode, long names, edge cases like empty segments (but still valid),
#   and combinations that exercise parent/child creation and lookup.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic given seed, but varied across calls.

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits

# Some Unicode ranges to spice up identifiers while remaining valid-ish names
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "β", "δ", "Ω", "你好", "привет", "こんにちは", "🙂", "αβ", "µ",
]

SEPARATORS = ["/", "."]
PREFIXES = ["::", None, ""]

# Reserved words or common identifiers to mix in
COMMON_NAMES = [
    "Player", "Enemy", "NPC", "Transform", "Renderable", "Physics",
    "Root", "World", "Scene", "System", "Module", "Child", "Parent",
]


def rand_ident(rng: random.Random, allow_unicode: bool = True) -> str:
    # Occasionally pick a common name or unicode sample
    roll = rng.random()
    if allow_unicode and roll < 0.25:
        return rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    if roll < 0.45:
        return rng.choice(COMMON_NAMES)
    # Otherwise construct a C-like identifier
    start = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    length = rng.randint(0, 12)
    middle = ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CONT) for _ in range(length))
    # Optional suffix digits
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        middle += str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
    return start + middle


def make_path_segments(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    segs: List[str] = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for i in range(n):
        seg = rand_ident(rng, allow_unicode=True)
        # Occasionally create repeated names to test ordered children/lookups
        if rng.random() < 0.1 and segs:
            seg = segs[-1]
        segs.append(seg)
    # Occasionally insert an empty segment between valid ones when using '/' to create
    # a path like "A//B" which in Flecs is treated as an empty identifier between.
    # But for robustness, keep mostly valid: only do this rarely.
    if rng.random() < 0.05 and len(segs) >= 2:
        idx = rng.randrange(1, len(segs))
        segs.insert(idx, "")
    return segs


def build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sep = rng.choice(SEPARATORS)
    prefix = rng.choice(PREFIXES)

    segs = make_path_segments(rng)

    # Optionally escape segments if using '.' to avoid special parsing in some setups
    # Here we just leave them as-is; Flecs supports arbitrary names.

    # Optionally append variant suffixes to last segment to create unique names
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        suffix_parts = []
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            suffix_parts.append(str(rng.randint(1, 100000)))
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            suffix_parts.append(rand_ident(rng))
        if suffix_parts:
            segs[-1] = f"{segs[-1]}_{'_'.join(suffix_parts)}"

    # Optionally include spaces or dashes in some segments to test name parsing
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        i = rng.randrange(len(segs))
        segs[i] = segs[i] + rng.choice(["-X", " Y", "-01", " v2"])    

    path = sep.join(segs)

    # With some probability, apply a root prefix '::' when prefix is chosen
    if prefix == "::":
        # Ensure single leading prefix
        path = "::" + path
    elif prefix == "":
        # Explicitly no prefix
        pass

    return path


def build_parent_child_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # For stubs that need separate parent and child names
    parent = rand_ident(rng)
    child = rand_ident(rng)
    # Occasionally create multi-segment child names to exercise add_path/lookups
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        child_path = build_path(rng)
    else:
        child_path = child
    return [parent, child_path]


def assemble_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    corpus: List[str] = []

    # Basic single identifiers
    for _ in range(5):
        corpus.append(rand_ident(rng))

    # Multi-segment paths with varying separators and prefixes
    for _ in range(10):
        corpus.append(build_path(rng))

    # Specific interesting cases
    corpus.extend([
        "Root/Child/GrandChild",
        "::Root/Child",
        "Scene.Main/Player_1",
        "Module.System",
        "世界/こんにちは",
        "Enemy-Boss/Phase_2",
        "Parent/Child v2",
    ])

    # Ensure some names that are likely unique each call
    for _ in range(5):
        corpus.append(f"{rng.choice(COMMON_NAMES)}_{rng.randint(0, 1_000_000)}")

    # Parent-child combos: return as separate entries to feed successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    p, c = build_parent_child_names(rng)
    corpus.append(p)
    corpus.append(c)

    # Another path that is absolute root
    corpus.append("::" + build_path(rng).lstrip(":"))

    # Keep total combined under 4096 when joined
    return corpus


def encode_strings(strs: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with NUL separators so the fuzzer harness can split into consecutive FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads
    # Many fuzzers will read sequentially from the corpus buffer; NULs are safe string terminators.
    data = b"\x00".join(s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")[:512] for s in strs)
    # Guarantee buffer non-empty and within limit
    return data[:4096] if data else b"A"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = assemble_corpus(rng)
    return encode_strings(corpus)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: entity name string
# Requirements from stubs:
# - Used as parent name and child name
# - Passed to ecs_entity_init (as name) and ecs_add_path_w_sep (path segment)
# - Should be a single-segment name (no path separators for both "/" and "." and potentially others like "::")
# - Interesting inputs should cover: ASCII, unicode, numeric, underscores, long names, names starting with digits,
#   names with escape-worthy characters but not separators, repeated names, and edge-ish lengths.
# - Avoid separators: '/', '.', '::' (we will avoid ':' entirely to be safe), and '\\' to avoid platform path semantics.
# - Also avoid NUL and control chars that could be treated as separators/invalid C strings.
# - Keep total buffer <= 4096 bytes.
#
# FUZZER expectations:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() will read from the provided buffer. Typically frameworks split on NUL or length-prefix.
#   As we don't control exact protocol, we will provide two newline-separated strings that are C-string safe
#   and contain no embedded NUL. Newlines are commonly accepted delimiters; if the harness reads as C-strings
#   it will still get the first up to NUL (we include no NULs). If it slices arbitrarily, having multiple
#   distinct segments increases chance that two calls get different values.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a corpus of candidate name strings covering variety.
# - Randomly assemble 2-5 names separated by '\n'.
# - Ensure each name length between 1 and 128 by default, with occasional extremes up to ~1024 but total <= 4096.
# - Characters allowed set excludes separators: '/','.',':','\\'. We also exclude whitespace other than space,
#   but we will include spaces in some names to exercise escaping paths (the API supports escaping).
# - Include some Unicode letters that are not separators.

SAFE_ASCII = (
    [c for c in string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_ -@#$%^&*()+={}[];,!?'~"]
)
# Remove potentially problematic ones: separators and backslash and quotes that might be path tokens in Flecs
for ch in ['/', '.', ':', '\\', '"']:
    if ch in SAFE_ASCII:
        SAFE_ASCII.remove(ch)

# A small set of Unicode samples (no separators)
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "Æon", "naïve", "café", "über", "Δelta", "πratio", "тест", "名字", "名前", "이름",
    "नाम", "όνομα", "Tên", "ชื่อ", "اسم", "שם", "שֵׁם", "ชื่อเรื่อง",
]

# Edge-case single characters (but still valid)
EDGE_SINGLE = list("_-$@!?") + ["a", "Z", "0"]

# Build blocks without separators
def rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, allow_space: bool = True, allow_unicode: bool = True) -> str:
    # Occasionally pick from predefined unicode samples
    pick_unicode = allow_unicode and rng.random() < 0.2
    if pick_unicode:
        base = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        # Optionally append a safe suffix
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            suf_len = rng.randint(0, 8)
            suffix = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(suf_len))
            base = base + suffix
        return base

    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure first char is not a space to avoid leading separator-like visuals
    first_choices = [c for c in SAFE_ASCII if c != ' ']
    name_chars = [rng.choice(first_choices)]

    pool = SAFE_ASCII if allow_space else [c for c in SAFE_ASCII if c != ' ']
    for _ in range(length - 1):
        name_chars.append(rng.choice(pool))

    return ''.join(name_chars)

def interesting_names(rng: random.Random, target_total: int) -> List[str]:
    names: List[str] = []

    # Curated interesting fixed cases
    fixed = [
        "Parent", "Child", "entity", "Entity_1", "child-01", "x", "X123", "name_with_spaces",
        "trailing_space ", " leading_space", "multi  space", "dash-name", "underscore_name",
        "camelCaseName", "PascalCaseName", "snake_case_123", "kebab-case-123", "mix3dAlphaNum",
    ]
    # Remove any with separators we banned
    fixed = [s for s in fixed if all(ch not in s for ch in ['/', '.', ':', '\\'])]
    names.extend(fixed)

    # Unicode samples
    names.extend(UNICODE_SAMPLES[:])

    # Edge short and long
    names.append(''.join(['A']))
    names.append(''.join(['Z']*32))
    names.append(''.join(['n']*63))

    # Randomly generate additional names until target_total approx reached
    while len(names) < target_total:
        # Mix lengths
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            # Longish but keep overall budget
            n = rand_name(rng, 32, 96, allow_space=True)
        elif rng.random() < 0.30:
            # Very short
            n = rng.choice(EDGE_SINGLE)
        else:
            n = rand_name(rng, 3, 24, allow_space=True)
        names.append(n)

    # Shuffle for variety
    rng.shuffle(names)
    return names


def pack_strings_as_newline_separated(strings: List[str], max_bytes: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Join with newlines and ensure within max_bytes; if too large, trim list
    out = []
    total = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        # ensure no NULs (shouldn't be any), and strip separators if slipped in
        if b"\x00" in b:
            b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"")
        # Skip if would exceed
        need = len(b) + (1 if out else 0)
        if total + need > max_bytes:
            break
        if out:
            out.append(b"\n")
            total += 1
        out.append(b)
        total += len(b)
    # Ensure at least two lines to feed two FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
    if out.count(b"\n") == 0:
        # Not enough, add a duplicate short safe name
        extra = rand_name(rng, 3, 8)
        eb = extra.encode('utf-8')
        if total + 1 + len(eb) <= max_bytes:
            out.append(b"\n")
            out.append(eb)
    return b"".join(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many names to include (2 to 40), keeping size cap in mind
    target = rng.randint(6, 24)
    names = interesting_names(rng, target)

    # Optionally bias first two entries to be simple and common
    simple1 = rand_name(rng, 3, 12, allow_space=False, allow_unicode=False)
    simple2 = rand_name(rng, 3, 12, allow_space=False, allow_unicode=False)
    # Ensure no separators and not identical to increase variety
    if simple2 == simple1:
        simple2 = simple2 + "_"
    # Put them at front to increase chance FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls valid C-like identifiers
    names = [simple1, simple2] + names

    buf = pack_strings_as_newline_separated(names, 4096, rng)
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: identifier prefix string
# Goal: produce short, valid, interesting C strings used as name prefixes.
# Characteristics to exercise:
# - common C prefixes ("ecs_", "ECS_", "flecs_", "comp_", "sys_")
# - empty string and single-char prefixes
# - mixed case, unicode (UTF-8), digits, punctuation that is valid in paths
# - separators like "::", ".", "/", "_", "-"
# - long but bounded strings
# - repeated characters, palindromes
# - whitespace and leading/trailing underscores/dots
# - non-ASCII letters to check UTF-8 handling
# Constraints:
# - Return bytes representing a NUL-terminated C string buffer, as FUZZ_PARAM_STR likely
#   reads raw bytes for the initial corpus; provide without embedded NULs so c_str() stops only at end.
# - Keep total size <= 4096.

ASCII_LETTERS = string.ascii_letters
DIGITS = string.digits
SAFE_PUNCT = "_-.:/$"  # plausible in prefixes/namespaces
WHITESPACE = " \t"

STATIC_INTERESTING: List[str] = [
    "",                # empty prefix
    "_",               # single underscore
    ".",               # dot
    "::",              # C++-style scope
    "/",               # path-like
    "ecs_",
    "ECS_",
    "flecs_",
    "Comp_",
    "sys_",
    "mod_",
    "__",
    "..",
    "-",
    "~",               # unusual but valid ASCII
    "💡",               # emoji utf-8
    "π_",              # non-ascii letter
    "名前_",            # CJK
    "префикс_",        # Cyrillic
    "नाम_",             # Devanagari
    "_private_",
    "test.",
    "org.example.",
    "com.game.",
    "v1_",
    "v2::",
    "__internal::",
    ".hidden_",
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = ASCII_LETTERS + DIGITS + SAFE_PUNCT
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_with_spaces(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = ASCII_LETTERS + DIGITS + SAFE_PUNCT + WHITESPACE
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    # Occasionally trim or pad spaces to test leading/trailing ws
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = (" " * rng.randint(0, 2)) + s + (" " * rng.randint(0, 2))
    return s

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "μ_", "ß_", "Å_", "ñ_", "á_", "Ø_", "Ž_", "汉字_", "日本語_", "한국_", "😀_",
]

def _rand_hybrid(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    parts = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.5:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, max(1, (max_len // count))))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(["::", ".", "_", "/"]))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    # Bound length
    if len(s) < min_len:
        s += _rand_ascii(rng, min_len - len(s), min_len - len(s))
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s

def _palindrome(rng: random.Random, min_half: int, max_half: int) -> str:
    half = _rand_ascii(rng, min_half, max_half)
    mid = '' if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.choice(ASCII_LETTERS + DIGITS)
    return half + mid + half[::-1]

def _ensure_no_nul(s: str) -> str:
    return s.replace('\x00', '')

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide a strategy bucket
    bucket = rng.random()

    if bucket < 0.20:
        # Pick a static interesting sample
        s = rng.choice(STATIC_INTERESTING)
    elif bucket < 0.40:
        # Random short ascii prefix
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8)
    elif bucket < 0.60:
        # Random medium ascii/space/punct
        s = _rand_with_spaces(rng, 0, 24)
    elif bucket < 0.75:
        # Hybrid with unicode and separators
        s = _rand_hybrid(rng, 1, 32)
    elif bucket < 0.85:
        # Repeated character or pattern
        ch = rng.choice(["_", ".", "-", ":", "/", "x", "A"])
        n = rng.randint(1, 64)
        s = ch * n
    elif bucket < 0.93:
        # Palindrome
        s = _palindrome(rng, 1, 12)
    else:
        # Construct domain-like or namespace chain
        parts = []
        count = rng.randint(1, 5)
        for i in range(count):
            base = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 10)).lower()
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                base += '_'
            parts.append(base)
        sep = rng.choice([".", "::", "/"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else "_"
        s = sep.join(parts)
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            s += sep

    # Occasionally add common known prefixes/suffixes to probe behavior
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        affixes = ["ecs_", "ECS_", "flecs_", "sys_", "comp_", "mod_"]
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = rng.choice(affixes) + s
        else:
            s = s + rng.choice(["_impl", "_v1", "::detail", ".internal"])  

    # Enforce max total length well below 4096
    max_len = 512
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]

    s = _ensure_no_nul(s)

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes; do not append explicit NUL as FUZZ_PARAM_STR likely handles raw buffer.
    # However to be safe for C APIs expecting c_str(), we avoid embedded NULs and rely on buffer end.
    return s.encode('utf-8')
